Jean Sibelius was a Finnish composer, born in 1865, whose music gave voice to the Finnish nation in its struggle for independence.

He drew on the Kalevala for works such as the Kullervo symphony and the Lemminkäinen suite. His tone poem Finlandia of 1899 was written as a protest against Russian efforts to curb Finnish autonomy, and became an unofficial anthem. He wrote seven symphonies, among the most performed of the 20th century, and a famous violin concerto.

The state gave him a pension, and from 1904 he lived at Ainola, his home outside Helsinki. He wrote almost nothing in his last thirty years. He is a national hero of Finland, tied to the independence his music helped inspire.
sum: Jean Sibelius was a Finnish composer, born in 1865, whose music gave voice to the Finnish nation in its struggle for independence.
